headline: Fuel-Tax Relief Moves Closer After Dubai Crude Breaches Legal Trigger
seoTitle: Fuel-Tax Relief Trigger Breached as Dubai Crude Average Hits $99.41 | FMB News
seoDescription: The DOE certified a 30-day Dubai crude average of $99.41 per barrel, clearing a legal trigger for possible temporary petroleum excise-tax relief. No suspension has been approved yet.
deck: The Department of Energy has certified that the 30-day Dubai crude average exceeded the $80 threshold under Republic Act No. 12316, moving a possible excise-tax intervention to the DBCC and the President.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Department of Energy has formally certified that the 30-day average price of Dubai crude reached $99.41 per barrel from August 13 to September 11, exceeding the $80 threshold set under Republic Act No. 12316.
Energy Secretary Sharon Garin said the certification was transmitted to the Development Budget Coordination Committee for consideration.
The certification does not itself suspend or reduce fuel excise taxes. A recommendation from economic managers and a subsequent presidential decision are still required.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The certification followed another large round of Philippine pump-price increases and a wider surge in international crude prices linked to Middle East supply disruptions.
Republic Act No. 12316 created a mechanism that allows temporary petroleum excise-tax relief when the prescribed international oil-price threshold is met, subject to the process set by law.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Fuel costs affect more than motorists. Sustained increases can feed into transport, logistics and food-distribution costs, making the government’s next decision relevant to household inflation as well as public revenue.
The important distinction is that the legal trigger has been met, but tax relief has not yet been approved.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for the DBCC recommendation, the scope and duration of any proposed tax adjustment, and a formal presidential decision.
Further movement in global crude prices will also determine whether the pressure behind the policy debate continues to intensify.

sources.title: $80 oil trigger breached, opening door to fuel tax suspension

verificationNotes: DOE certification of the $99.41 30-day Dubai crude average and transmission to the DBCC were verified in September 15 reporting.
Republic Act No. 12316 was checked directly for the $80 threshold and the required DBCC/DOE/presidential process.
The article explicitly states that no new excise-tax suspension has been approved yet.
